text.title: Content Refresh SOP Worked Example
text.summary: One complete playbook step for two evergreen guides scored over 90-day windows from a persisted export: a 19-month-old checklist post with impressions down 32 percent and 3.1 positions of decay that goes through all nine refresh steps with a baseline and a day-90 re-score, and a 31-month-old definition post inside every threshold recorded as leave, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the playbook step as usually written and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: A B2B SaaS blog runs its quarterly refresh cycle on 2026-04-28 with thresholds of -20 percent impressions, 2 positions of decay and a 30 percent query-mix change, comparing the last 90 days with the 90 before from a persisted Search Console export. Two evergreen guides are in the queue.

example.title: one refresh, one leave
example.note: Both URLs are evergreen and older than 12 months; a March 2026 launch post in the same inventory was left out because it is 3 months old (r-eligibility-evergreen-12-months). Each row carries all three sources for two 90-day windows, and the 6-month span fits inside the 16 months Search Console keeps, though the export is used anyway (r-one-dataset-gsc-ga4-rank). `impressions_trend_pct` is (38,400 - 56,500) / 56,500 = -32.0 and `position_decay_positions` is 7.8 - 4.7 = 3.1, both past the thresholds written in `thresholds` and `decision_branches` before scoring; the intent note records a 9 percent query-mix change, under the 30 percent line, so the branch routes to refresh rather than kill (r-three-signals-with-thresholds). The second URL is inside every threshold and is recorded as `leave` with the reason and a November review date, so the next cycle skips it (r-four-verdicts-exhaustive). The refresh keeps the slug; `dateModified` moved because steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 changed the body, and the title stayed because the intent did not shift (r-refresh-keeps-url-honest-date). All nine checklist steps have a checkable exit criterion; steps 4 and 6, the ones that move rankings, name what was added and which newer posts now link in (r-nine-step-checklist-complete). The baseline is the 28 days after the May 6 publication and `reevaluation_at` is August 4, exactly 90 days later (r-baseline-and-90-day-reevaluation). No consolidate or kill in this cycle, so those blocks are absent.

example.title: the same queue as usually handled
example.note: What the validator prints: the 24-month span is read from the Search Console UI, which keeps 16 months (r-one-dataset-gsc-ga4-rank); the first URL is 8 months old (r-eligibility-evergreen-12-months); its refresh has `url_unchanged: false`, `date_modified_updated: true` with `substantive_change: false`, a 2-item checklist instead of 9, a 7-day baseline and a re-evaluation 14 days out (r-refresh-keeps-url-honest-date, r-nine-step-checklist-complete, r-baseline-and-90-day-reevaluation); the kill returns 301 to the homepage, stays in the sitemap and keeps its internal links (r-kill-returns-410-never-homepage); and `decision_branches` has one branch with no number in it and no branch for position decay or intent shift (r-three-signals-with-thresholds). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks add: `prior_days` 120 does not equal `trailing_days` 365; the first URL's signals do not recompute from its dataset (the export gives -32.0 percent and 3.1 positions, not -12.0 and 1.0); and `reevaluation_at` is not 90 days after `published_at`. What the reviewer sees: a date bump under a new slug that will pass through a redirect and lose its position for weeks (date-bump-without-change, refresh-changes-url), and a homepage redirect that Search Console will list as a soft 404 (kill-redirected-to-homepage).
